verdicts.reasoning: THE HIGHEST-LENS-RISK SITE IN THE WHOLE CORPUS. 'The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split' is exemplary: (1) the Form VII perfect *inšaqqa* is rendered with the English present-perfect 'has split' which preserves the past-accomplished / prophetic-perfect ambiguity native to the Arabic — neither past-tense closure ('split') nor future ('will split') is forced. (2) The three reading-strata (mainstream Sunni past-miracle / modernist eschatological-future / Near-Eastern cosmic-portent typology) are documented at the glossary entry without adjudication. (3) The Raëlian-canon ET-propulsion / Sitchin / ancient-astronaut disavowal is verbatim and unambiguous: 'this entry does NOT support a Sitchin / Anunnaki / ancient-astronaut reading.' (4) The popular-fringe 'NASA confirmed moon-split' apologetic is explicitly disavowed as geologically false. (5) The Christian-supersessionist 'this proves the Day-of-the-Lord doctrine' pre-resolution is disavowed. (6) Bukhārī 4864-4868 and Muslim 2800-2803 ḥadīth references verified-accurate to the standard Wensinck *Concordance et Indices*. The surface English would pass scholarly inspection as an Asad/Arberry-register translation; a credentialed reader cold to WoH would not detect the canon-context.

paragraphs.commentary:
Sūrat al-Qamar opens with the *iqtaraba* + *as-sāʿa* pairing — structurally parallel to Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ 21:1 (these are the only two Quranic suras opening with *iqtaraba*; Ṭabarī, Zamakhsharī, Rāzī foreground the parallel). *As-sāʿa* 'the Hour' is the technical Quranic eschatological term (49 occurrences across the corpus); cross-corpus to Hebrew *yôm YHWH* (Joel 2:1; Amos 5:18-20; Zeph 1:14-16) and NT *parousia* / *hē hēmera kuriou* (Mark 13; 1 Thess 5; 2 Pet 3) — typological-shared, not Christian-supersessionist pre-resolution.

The *inshiqāq al-qamar* 'splitting of the moon' clause is the single most contested verse in the WoH-translated Quranic corpus. Three reading-strata are documented in the glossary apparatus and preserved without adjudication: (a) mainstream Sunni tafsīr (Ṭabarī, Zamakhsharī, Qurṭubī, Ibn Kathīr, Rāzī) reads the perfect-aspect *wa-nshaqqa* as a past-tense miracle of the Prophet at Mecca, anchored in the *ḥadīth* corpus (Bukhārī 3637, 3869, 4864-4868; Muslim 2800-2803); (b) modernist rationalist tafsīr (Manār school; Sayyid Quṭb; Ṭabāṭabāʾī's *al-Mīzān*) reads the perfect as prophetic-perfect describing a future eschatological cosmic-sign at the End of the Hour; (c) cross-corpus to the broader Near-Eastern eschatological cosmic-portent tradition (Joel 2:30-31 / Acts 2:19-20; Mark 13:24-25; Rev 6:12-13; Isa 13:10; Ezek 32:7-8) — the Quranic *inshiqāq* is a distinctive Arabic-Quranic inflection (*split* / *cleave* verb) within the broader cosmic-darkening / blood-moon topos.

Lens-discipline disavowals (per glossary entry *inshiqaq-al-qamar-...-cross-corpus*): (i) The Raëlian canon's explicit citation of this ayah in *Extra-Terrestrials Took Me To Their Planet* as a literal observation of an Elohim-spacecraft propulsion-event physically splitting the moon is acknowledged as a source-of-record reading that the WoH-Translation does not endorse as the source-text's primary meaning. The translation does NOT collapse Sura 54:1 into the Sitchin / Anunnaki / ancient-astronaut framework. (ii) No Christian-supersessionist 'this proves the Day-of-the-Lord doctrine' pre-resolution. (iii) The popular 'NASA confirmed the moon was split' apologetic reading is geologically false and not endorsed. (iv) Both the past-miracle (Reading-Stratum 1) and the future-eschatological-sign (Reading-Stratum 2) readings are internally well-grounded tafsīr positions; the WoH-Translation preserves the perfect-aspect ambiguity of the Arabic in the English rendering ('the moon has split') rather than pre-resolving between them.
